label: EXPLORATORY_PILOT
research_question: Do funding-conditioned features improve out-of-sample probabilistic calibration (Brier score primary, log-loss secondary) of modeled liquidation-boundary breach risk over an RV-only baseline across multiple chronological holdouts, and is any effect distinguishable from a funding-permutation placebo?

outcome.explicit_caveat: Never call these observed liquidations; they are modeled boundary crossings on cached 1h mark prices.

label_pipeline.entry: close of 1h mark bar t (known at t)
label_pipeline.breach_rule: long breached if min(path) <= long_boundary; short breached if max(path) >= short_boundary

features.standardization: train-only z-score (mean/sd from training rows only)
features.causality: all features computed from information available at or before entry bar t close

estimation.family: stdlib IRLS logistic regression with intercept

metrics.paired_delta: delta_brier = brier_B0 - brier_Bm (positive means funding model better calibrated)
metrics.pooling: equal-weight mean of delta_brier over all 12 scenarios

uncertainty.method: UTC-day block bootstrap, percentile CI95, 2000 reps

placebo.method: deterministic permutation of the funding series across entry timestamps, identical pipeline
placebo.report: mean and percentile CI95 of delta_brier distribution

calibration_table: predicted vs observed breach rate by predicted-risk decile for the best model, per holdout
materiality_floor: B1 or B2 beats B0 (delta_brier > 0 with bootstrap CI95 lower bound > 0) in >= 2 of 3 holdouts on the primary scenario L10|long|H24 AND real |mean delta_brier| exceeds placebo |mean delta_brier|. Otherwise report an honest negative.
sealed_month_policy: 2024-10 onward are sealed and are not read; only 2024-04..2024-09 labels and 2024-03..2024-09 marks/funding are read.
